entries.root_cause: JavaScript regex-literal eligibility in comment masking and assignment scanning was inferred only from punctuation, so a regex beginning after an expression-leading keyword such as typeof could be misread as division and a double slash inside its character class could then be masked as a line comment, erasing downstream secret provenance.
horizontal_audit: regex literals after void return and yield
regex character classes containing double slash

entries.root_cause: Secret-sink invocation equivalence covered optional direct calls and ordinary call/apply helper invocation but omitted optional invocation of the call/apply helper itself, allowing the same governed sink to receive raw credentials through call?.(...) or apply?.(...).

Static computed sink recognition accepted bracket access only when the bracket followed the receiver directly, so JavaScript optional computed member access with the semantically equivalent receiver?.[member] form escaped sink classification even when followed by an optional call.

SQL-bearing tagged-template extraction accepted bare and dotted tag expressions but not statically computed or balanced-grouped member tags, allowing authority-changing SQL passed to a governed execution call to evade SQL-surface classification.
horizontal_audit: query execute exec run and sql calls
